title: Rage, Denial, Hope
program_note: This work is meant to portray the range of emo­tions one might feel if faced with conflicting reports of the death of a close family member — of which Rage, Denial, and Hope are three of the many possible.  In the face of such a situation, these emotions co-ex-ist to varying degrees, the relative strength of each changing over time.  One might think of the ensemble as having two parts:  the harp and the flute rep­resent the body and the more “visceral” emotions, while the vio-la represents the heart and the more “sorrowful” or “loving” emotions.  These roles interact and affect one another throughout the work.  The feelings progress from the “unfocused” rage at the beginning, overlaid with an emerging sadness, to the sense of determination found at the end.  Rage, Denial, Hope was commissioned by and written for the Debussy Trio, and was completed in October, 1995.
